feedback.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+8x+50y=129?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+8x+50y & =129 \\ {x}^{2}+8x-5{y}^{2}+50y & =129 \\ {x}^{2}+8x-5[{y}^{2}-10y] & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16-5[(y-5)^{2}-25] & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16-5(y-5)^{2}+125 & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-5(y-5)^{2} & =129+16-125 \\ (x+4)^{2}-5(y-5)^{2} & =20 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{20}-\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-4,5).$
